content.text:
No, $18k isn't right. It's a sum that counts the same spending many times. Here's where the number comes from.

**The source.** Every figure comes from Claude Code itself. At the end of each run it prints a `result` line, and the app saves that line in the run's `.json` record. That line has a `total_cost_usd` field. I only added those up; I didn't calculate any prices myself.

**Why $18k is wrong.** `total_cost_usd` isn't the cost of that run. It's the running total for the whole conversation so far. Tasks keep carrying on the same conversation, so each run's figure includes every run before it. One conversation reports $0.43, then $1.45, $2.61 … up to $21.23 over 14 runs. Adding those up counts the first run 14 times, the second 13 times, and so on. That's how 4-turn runs lasting under a minute ended up at about $300 each.

**The better figure is about $1,900.** For each run I took only how much its conversation's total went up since the previous run. That comes to about $1,883: $1,834 for tasks and $49 for questions. It's still not exact, because 109 runs started a new total partway through and I counted those in full.

**Even that isn't what you paid.** `total_cost_usd` is Claude Code's estimate of what the tokens would cost at API prices. If you use Claude Code with a Pro or Max subscription, you pay the flat subscription, not this amount. It only matches real charges if Claude Code is billed to an API key.

**What drives it.** Most of the cost is cache reads, about 2.6 billion tokens. Every turn re-reads the conversation's full context from the cache, and with long conversations on a 1M-context model that adds up fast. Output is only about 6.4 million tokens.

The app's own usage display probably has the same problem: it treats each result's total as that run's alone, so it likely shows inflated spend too. I can fix that if you'd like.
